[[File:Isql 3.jpg|thumb|250px|Peter Mittelstaedt (right) And Carl Friedrich von Weizsäcker (left) During the International Symposium on Quantum Logic, Cologne 1984]]
'''Peter Mittelstaedt''' pseudonym '''Karl Rottmann''' (born November 24, 1929, in Leipzig - November 21, 2014, in Erftstadt), was a German physicist, philosopher, and scientific theorist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wirtrauern.de/Traueranzeige/Peter-Mittelstaedt|title=Traueranzeige Peter Mittelstaedt|accessdate=2015-12-18|date=26 November 2014|publisher=[[Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Quantum-Matter-Spacetime: Peter Mittelstaedt's Contributions to Physics and Its Foundations | url=http://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/42664/1/Mittelstaedt.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719080045/http://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/42664/1/Mittelstaedt.pdf | archive-date=2018-07-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9789400755925|doi = 10.1007/978-94-007-5593-2|title = Rational Reconstructions of Modern Physics|year = 2013|last1 = Mittelstaedt|first1 = Peter|isbn = 978-94-007-5592-5}}</ref>

==Biography==
After studying physics at the universities of Jena, Bonn, and Göttingen, with a doctorate in theoretical physics in Göttingen in 1956 with [[Werner Heisenberg]], Mittelstaedt had research stays at CERN<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mittelstaedt |first=P. |year=1958 |title=On the rearrangement energy of nuclear matter |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0029558258903298 |journal=Nuclear Physics |language=en |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=116–123 |doi=10.1016/0029-5582(58)90329-8|bibcode=1958NucPh...9..116M |url-access=subscription }}</ref> in Geneva and at MIT in Cambridge, US, and at the then [[Max Planck Institute for Physics and Astrophysics]] in Munich, where he also completed his habilitation in 1961. In 1965, Mittelstaedt became a Professor of Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Cologne]], his main areas of work were philosophy of natural science, philosophy of science, and logic as well as the basics of relativity and quantum theory. In 1968, and 1969 he was Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, Rector of the University in 1970 and 1971, Vice-Rector from 1971 to 1973, and later Vice-Rector for Research in Cologne. Mittelstaedt retired in 1995. He was also chairman of the board of directors of the publishing house [[Bibliographisches Institut]]. Mittelstaedt died at the age of 84 and was buried in [[Erftstadt-Lechenich]] on November 29, 2014, after a memorial service.

He is known for monographs on physics philosophy, where he was influenced by [[Paul Lorenzen]] and his [[operationalism]] and pursued a justification of quantum mechanics via [[quantum logic]], for which he tried to provide a physical interpretation in his later work.<ref>Zum Beispiel Mittelstaedt, Quantum Physics and Classical Physics - in the Light of Quantum Logic, [http://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0211021 Arxiv 2003] und Mittelstaedt, Rational Reconstructions of Modern Physics, Springer, 2. Auflage 2013</ref>

His total of 30 students,<ref>Eine vollständige Liste der 30 [[Dissertation|Doktorarbeiten]], die bei Peter Mittelstaedft angefertigt wurden, findet man in: Foundations of Physics 40 (2010), S. 1198–1199.</ref> who received their doctorate from 1966 to 1997 with him in Cologne, included [[Julian Barbour]], [[Hubertus von Grünberg]], [[Wolfgang Hillebrandt]], [[Heinz-Erich Wichmann]], [[Ernst-Walther Stachow]],<ref>Stachow war als Professor für Grundlagenfragen der Physik an der [[Universität zu Köln]] tätig und ist Verfasser zahlreicher Arbeiten zur [[Quantenlogik]].</ref> [[Franz Josef Burghardt]], [[Hans-Joachim Blome]]<ref>Der Astrophysiker Hans-Joachim Blome entwickelte gemeinsam mit [[Wolfgang Priester]] das [[Big Bounce]]-Modell zur Entstehung des Universums.</ref> and [[Paul Busch (physicist)|Paul Busch]].<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10701-018-0206-8 | doi=10.1007/s10701-018-0206-8 | title=Paul Busch 1955–2018 | date=2018 | last1=Gudder | first1=Stan | last2=Lahti | first2=Pekka | last3=Loveridge | first3=Leon | journal=Foundations of Physics | volume=48 | issue=9 | pages=1128–1130 | bibcode=2018FoPh...48.1128G }}</ref>

His grandfather was the lawyer at the Imperial Court of Justice Johannes Mittelstaedt and his great-grandfather was the Imperial Judicial Councilor and journalist [[Otto Mittelstaedt]] (1834–1899).

== Publications ==
=== Books ===
* as Karl Rottmann: ''Mathematische Formelsammlung'', BI Wissenschaftsverlag 1960<ref>Eintrag im [[Register anonymer und pseudonymer Werke]], veröffentlicht im Bundesanzeiger am 17. Januar 2013.</ref>
* as Karl Rottmann: ''Winkelfunktionen und logarithmische Funktionen'', BI Wissenschaftsverlag 1966 (Hochschultaschenbücher 113/113a)
* ''Philosophische Probleme der modernen Physik'', BI 1963 (7. Aufl. 1989)
* ''Klassische Mechanik'', BI 1970 (2. Aufl. 1995)
* ''Die Sprache der Physik: Aufsätze und Vorträge'', BI 1972
* ''Der Zeitbegriff in der Physik. Physikalische und philosophische Untersuchungen zum Zeitbegriff in der klassischen und relativistischen Physik'', BI Wissenschaftsverlag 1976 (3. Aufl. 1989)
* ''Quantum Logic'', Dordrecht, Reidel 1978
* ''Sprache und Realität in der modernen Physik'', BI 1986
* with Paul Busch, Pekka J. Lahti: ''The Quantum Theory of Measurement'', Springer, Lecturenotes in Physics, 1991, 2. Auflage 1996
* ''The Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics and the Measurement Process'', Cambridge University Press 1998 (paperback 2004)
* with [[Paul Weingartner|Paul A. Weingartner]]: ''Laws of Nature'', Springer 2005
* ''Rational Reconstructions of Modern Physics'', Springer, Dordrecht 2011, {{ISBN|978-94-007-0076-5}}.

=== Editor (excerpt) ===
* with Pekka J. Lahti: ''Symposium on the Foundations of Modern Physics'', 1985, 1987, 1990
* with Paul Busch und Pekka J. Lahti: ''Symposium on the Foundations of Modern Physics'', 1993
